title: Good/Bad Coherence Grammar Shows Cross-Domain Consilience
claim: The Lane 4 atom ledger shows repeated cross-domain convergence around a good/bad grammar: good, righteousness, truth, coherence, fruit, grace, and restoration cluster around alignment with a truth-bearing standard, while bad, sin, corruption, decoherence, vice, collapse, bondage, and propagation cluster around misalignment, degradation, or parasitic spread. This is consilience candidate evidence, not a mere science hedge and not yet a formal proof of theological identity.
assumptions: The Lane 4 atom ledger is accepted as the source corpus for this audit.
Repeated independent convergence across named domains can create consilience candidate evidence.
Consilience is weaker than formal isomorphism and stronger than casual analogy.
definitions: Consilience candidate: a cross-domain convergence pattern that appears independently across multiple lanes strongly enough to demand explanation, while remaining below formal isomorphism or identity.
Good/alignment cluster: goodness, righteousness, truth, coherence, fruit, grace, and restoration.
Bad/degradation cluster: badness, sin, corruption, decoherence, vice, collapse, bondage, and propagation.
equations: good / righteousness / truth / coherence / fruit -> alignment with a truth-bearing standard
bad / sin / corruption / decoherence / vice -> misalignment, degradation, collapse, or parasitic propagation
judgment / measurement / light / ledger -> exposure of alignment or misalignment
grace / restoration / atonement / fruit -> repair, reset, reintegration, or restored coherence
negative_guards: Do not call this Lean-proved theology.
Do not call every row formal isomorphism.
Do not treat science-language resemblance as automatic canon.
Do not hide the theological implication: repeated independent convergence is consilience candidate evidence.
Do not promote to identity until necessary/sufficient properties, operations, relations, and countermodels have been tested.
kill_conditions: The matching rows collapse into a single inherited vocabulary source rather than independent convergence.
The motifs fail relation-preservation review across domains.
Rival readings explain the pattern with fewer assumptions and no loss of explanatory power.
Good/alignment and bad/degradation clusters cannot be operationally distinguished under review.
The audit is shown to be keyword selection rather than structural preservation.
